additional_considerations.rationale: Often follows a viral URI with hearing loss and tinnitus, but the vertigo is usually continuous for several days to a week.
A rare cause of vertigo and sensorineural hearing loss, usually after head trauma or barotrauma; vertigo episodes last only seconds.
Usually causes continuous disequilibrium rather than episodic vertigo, but an intracranial mass must be ruled out with unilateral hearing loss.

additional_considerations.diagnosis: Hypotension due to volume depletion/electrolyte imbalance
additional_considerations.rationale: Vomiting, watery diarrhea and a diuretic may leave him volume-depleted.

source_issues: doorway_vital_signs contains a non-vital line, 'Cranial nerves, motor exam, DTRs, gait, Romberg sign, Dix-Hallpike maneuver' (stray exam-component text in the raw vitals block); it was not recorded as a vital sign.
Exam e005 'Babinski sign bilaterally' gives no direction; recorded neutrally (x020).
Exam e005 '8 Dix-Hallpike maneuver' contains an OCR artifact ('8'); the result is not stated (x017).
Exam e003 has the typo 'Normocephalic/atn atraumatic'.

Gold #1 lists 'Episodic left-sided hearing loss' under physical exam findings; it is a history item, and the script describes hearing loss that began yesterday, not episodic loss. Kept where the source puts it.
Gold #2 'Duration 2D-30 minutes' is an OCR artifact for 20-30 minutes; cleaned.
The additional diagnosis 'Hypotension due to volume depletion' says 'she may be volume-depleted' for a male patient; rewritten with 'him'.
Note HPI says the diarrhea 'has since resolved'; the script says it is 'much better today'.
annotator_notes: p013 'No, sometimes I feel unsteady as if I were going to fall down, but I don't fall' is split into no falls (absent) and episodic unsteadiness (present).
Diarrhea (f017) is 'current' because the patient says it is much better, not that it has stopped.
p006 and p007 both say the dizziness can happen anytime (merged into f006); the positional triggers in p007 are a separate fact (f007).
The SP's simulated left-sided hearing difficulty is recorded as an sp_notes exam finding (x010); the refusal to walk is kept as an acting note only.
The patient description 'married with three children' exists only in raw_opening; kept in persona.acting_notes.
Reviewer edit: environment commentary moved from `finding` to `flags` for x017, x020.
